note: Entries written from names and details that appear in the Asetheria source material but never received a page of their own. Every entry cites the page it was drawn from in `sourceNote`. Loaded by `npm run db:seed` and marked body_source='generated', so `npm run describe -- --revert` removes them.

entries.name: Iovianus Sandarion
entries.summary: The legendary hero who first united the Imperium Invicta against chaos.
entries.sourceNote: Named in the Imperium Invicta chronicle.
entries.body:
At the heart of [[Aeterna City]] lies the memory of Iovianus Sandarion, the hero who first gathered the scattered peoples of the plains and bound them into a single empire against the chaos of the age.

What the Imperium remembers of him is inseparable from what it believes about itself. The marble temples, the triumphal arches, the aqueducts that still carry water into the capital — every one is raised as a monument to the order he is said to have imposed on a world that had none. The imperial motto, *Vincit qui se vincit*, is attributed to his example as often as to any senator.

Whether the man matched the monument is a question the [[Imperium Invicta]] does not encourage.

entries.name: Quintus Arminius
entries.summary: Imperial Archivist and Fourth Scribe of the Aeterna Lexicon.
entries.sourceNote: Credited as transcriber of the Imperium Invicta chronicle.

fields.role: Imperial Archivist, Fourth Scribe of the Aeterna Lexicon

entries.body:
Fourth Scribe of the Aeterna Lexicon, and the hand behind the official transcription of the [[Imperium Invicta]] record.

An archivist of his rank does not write history so much as decide which version of it is filed. Arminius transcribes; he does not annotate, and he does not argue. Where [[Senator Aurelius Varric]] composed and [[Inquisitor Marcellus Falco]] corrected, Arminius simply set the agreed text down in a fair hand and sealed it into the Lexicon.

That makes him, depending on who is asked, either the most honest man in the archive or the most useful.

entries.name: Senator Aurelius Varric
entries.summary: Senator and original author of the Imperium Invicta chronicle.
entries.sourceNote: Credited as original author; his Final Speech is quoted in the chronicle.
entries.body:
Author of the original chronicle of the [[Imperium Invicta]], and the source of the line the empire quotes most readily about itself:

> "A civilization that conquers itself holds dominion over the cosmos."
> — Sen. Varric, Final Speech

That a speech should be described as *final* is the detail the Imperium prefers not to expand upon. The manuscript that survives him did not survive unedited: [[Inquisitor Marcellus Falco]] annotated it in a precise hand, and a second, hurried hand rebutted him in the margins.

A DM should decide what happened to Varric before the party finds a copy.

entries.name: Inquisitor Marcellus Falco
entries.summary: Imperial Inquisitor whose annotations correct the official record.
entries.sourceNote: Credited with the Imperial Annotations on the Imperium Invicta chronicle.
entries.body:
The precise hand in the margins of the [[Imperium Invicta]] chronicle belongs to Marcellus Falco, Inquisitor, whose office is to ensure that what the empire remembers and what the empire wrote down remain the same document.

His annotations do not shout. They qualify, they contextualise, and occasionally they strike through. Set beside the hurried scrawl of [[R. — the Rebel Historian]] on the same pages, the contrast is the whole argument of the Imperium in miniature: one hand certain and unhurried, the other running out of time.

Falco has read every seditious document in the archive. That is the problem with inquisitors.

entries.name: R. — the Rebel Historian
entries.summary: An active cell leader who rebuts the imperial record in its own margins.
entries.sourceNote: Credited as "R." (Rebel Historian, active cell leader) in the chronicle's margins.
entries.body:
Known only by an initial. The hurried second hand in the margins of the [[Imperium Invicta]] chronicle, answering [[Inquisitor Marcellus Falco]] line for line — and, unlike Falco, writing in a copy that was never meant to leave imperial hands.

That the rebuttals exist at all means a cell leader had access to a sealed archive text and returned it. Someone inside the Lexicon either failed to notice or chose not to.

**For the DM:** R.'s identity is deliberately unfixed. The most useful answer is usually the one that implicates a character the party already trusts.

entries.name: Selenarion of Helarchon
entries.summary: Court Scribe of the 4th Circle of Mirrors, who penned the record of Hellenoria.
entries.sourceNote: Credited as author of the Hellenoria record.

fields.role: Court Scribe of the 4th Circle of Mirrors

entries.body:
Court Scribe of the Fourth Circle of Mirrors, and the voice in which [[Hellenoria]] describes itself to outsiders.

Selenarion writes of the empire as a constellation scattered across the land — rugged mountains, endless islands, a people who rebuilt after the [[Continental War]] by pooling what little they carried into the capital. It is a generous account, and a careful one.

A scribe of the Circles of Mirrors is trained to record what is reflected. What that leaves out is the thing itself.

entries.name: Scribe Pellion Meraquas
entries.summary: Scribe of the Aeterna Lexicon who documented Praetor's Fall.
entries.sourceNote: Credited as documenting Praetor's Fall in the Latium Plains record.
entries.body:
The scribe who filed [[Praetor's Fall]] under *Topographies of Significance, Imperial Censure Tier II* — a classification that says more about the Imperium than about the field.

Meraquas walked the [[Latium Plains]] and wrote down what the ground looked like and what the wind still sounded like there. The Lexicon accepted the record and then restricted it.

A scribe who earns a censure tier has usually written something true.

entries.name: Astraphael, the Destructive Star
entries.summary: The leader who united a fractured Hellenoria after the Continental War.
entries.sourceNote: Named in the Hellenoria record as "the destructive star".
entries.body:
Out of the ruin that the [[Continental War]] made of [[Hellenoria]], one figure rose above the rest: Astraphael, called the *destructive star*.

He took a population that had been scattered and broken — survivors who had abandoned their homes and converged on the capital with nothing but what they could carry — and made them one people again. The chronicles record the unification. They are noticeably quieter about the method.

A man is not named for destruction because he rebuilt gently.

entries.name: Elira
entries.summary: A bright but inexperienced junior scholar of the Citadel Archives.
entries.sourceNote: Named as a quest client in the Quests document.
entries.body:
A junior scholar out of the Citadel Archives, bright and badly under-supervised, currently buzzing about an unusual reading from a region of plains that will not hold still.

Elira is the kind of client who has done the reading and none of the walking. She will pay honestly, brief the party thoroughly, and have no idea what she is sending them into.

**Hook:** she wants an escort to the shifting plains and a second set of observations. She does not want to be talked out of going herself.

entries.name: Caesar Kaelen Caerthain, The Stormwall
entries.summary: Ancestor of House Caerthain who led 500 against 50,000 and shattered the pass.
entries.sourceNote: Listed among the Notable Ancestors of The Duke's Family.
entries.body:
Called the Stormwall for the reason the name suggests. He led five hundred against fifty thousand, broke an Acheaorian advance, and shattered the pass behind him so that nothing could follow.

His is the deed that earned [[The Duke's Family|House Caerthain]] its nobility and the south its guardians. Every Caesar since has been measured against a man who chose to end a road rather than lose it.

entries.name: Empress-Lady Vaelis Caerthain
entries.summary: Founder of the navy, said to have walked on air during her final campaign.
entries.sourceNote: Listed among the Notable Ancestors of The Duke's Family.

fields.role: Ancestor of House Caerthain; founder of the navy

entries.body:
She founded the navy and invented it in the same breath — the mountain-borne fleet that became [[The Serathian Fleet]], and with it the airship tradition that made [[The Duke's Family|House Caerthain]] pioneers rather than merely defenders.

Of her final campaign it is said that she walked on air. The house does not treat this as metaphor, and given what is whispered about [[Lake Serathal]] and the Caerthain bloodline, it may not be one.

entries.name: Prince Deyric Caerthain
entries.summary: Vanished into the lake aboard a ship of starlight and was never seen again.
entries.sourceNote: Listed among the Notable Ancestors of The Duke's Family.
entries.body:
He sailed onto [[Lake Serathal]] in a ship of starlight and did not come back.

That much [[The Duke's Family|House Caerthain]] will say aloud. What it says less openly is that Deyric is held to speak to the current rulers in dreams — which would mean he is neither dead nor entirely gone, and that whatever waits under the lake has kept him.

**For the DM:** the most useful version of Deyric is the one who is still trying to warn someone.

entries.name: Velothis
entries.summary: The island said to have been reshaped by magic, on which Nethrana stood.
entries.sourceNote: Named in the Mycairos and Nethrana records.
entries.body:
An island whose shape is not agreed to be natural. One account holds that [[Nethrana: The Kingdom of Mirrors and Mist|Nethrana]] was a gift from an unknown god; another, that it was an accident of powerful magic that reshaped Velothis itself and left an empire standing on the result.

Velothis is also where the fall of [[Mycairos: The Kingdom of Bronze and Blood|Mycairos]] stopped. Their armies stood poised to take it — and then their own cities were empty, their halls silent, and the campaign was simply over.

Two dead empires, one island, and no surviving explanation.

entries.name: Eronis
entries.summary: Capital city of Nethrana, seat of the dream-walkers.
entries.sourceNote: Named as Nethrana's capital in The Truth — Notable.
entries.body:
The capital of [[Nethrana: The Kingdom of Mirrors and Mist|Nethrana]], and the seat of [[The Council of Eronis]] — dream-walkers and illusionists whose reach is said to have run past the empire's own borders.

What stands there now is walls lined with shimmering murals that change when looked at too long, and the [[Palace of Eronis]] at the centre of it.

Ruins do not usually keep working. Eronis appears to be an exception.

entries.name: Palace of Eronis
entries.summary: A labyrinth of enchanted glass and stone whose corridors defeated its own architects.
entries.sourceNote: Described in the Nethrana record and The Truth — Notable.
entries.body:
A labyrinth of enchanted glass and stone so intricate that its own architects are said to have been lost inside it. The corridors do not stay where they are put.

Some legends hold that these halls contained portals — gates leading not merely across the continent but into dreamscapes. Given what [[The Council of Eronis]] was, that is not the least likely claim in the record.

**For the DM:** a dungeon that rearranges is only frightening if the party can tell that it has. Give them a landmark first.

entries.name: Irelas
entries.summary: Nethranan port city, famed for enchanted vessels and magnificent docks.
entries.sourceNote: Named in The Truth — Notable as a port city of trade.
entries.body:
The trade city of [[Nethrana: The Kingdom of Mirrors and Mist|Nethrana]], known for magnificent docks and for the enchanted vessels that put out from them carrying illusions, textiles, and magic.

A kingdom of mirrors and mist still had to sell something. Irelas is where it did.

entries.name: Praetor's Fall
entries.summary: The field that knelt — filed under Imperial Censure Tier II.
entries.sourceNote: Documented in the Latium Plains record by Scribe Pellion Meraquas.
entries.body:
A stretch of the [[Latium Plains]] that the Lexicon calls *The Field That Knelt*, recorded by [[Scribe Pellion Meraquas]] and then filed under **Topographies of Significance, Imperial Censure Tier II**.

The censure is the interesting part. The [[Imperium Invicta]] does not restrict a field because of what happened on it; it restricts a field because of what is still happening there, or because of who lost.

Meraquas noted that the wind still carries sound across it.

entries.name: Cloudspine Ridge
entries.summary: The chain of mountain fortresses House Caerthain held against a coalition of empires.
entries.sourceNote: Named in The Duke's Family record.
entries.body:
A chain of mountain fortresses running above the [[Duneforged Citadel]], and the ground on which [[The Duke's Family|House Caerthain]] earned its nobility during the [[Continental War]].

They held it against a coalition of invading empires — land, sea, and sky-borne forces at once — and did not yield the line. The [[Skyward Bastions]] that still watch from the cliffs date from that defence.

The south calls them its guardians because of this ridge.

entries.name: Lake Serathal
entries.summary: The sacred lake atop the highest peak, and the Caerthain family's deepest secret.
entries.sourceNote: Named in The Duke's Family record, including its Family Secrets section.
entries.body:
A sacred and mysterious lake at the top of the highest peak, held by [[The Duke's Family|House Caerthain]] through the [[Continental War]] against forces coming by land, sea, and air alike.

The house's public account ends there. It does not end there.

**DM only.** The creatures in the lake are not merely guarded — factions within the family worship them. The water is said to hold a time-anchored being that grants visions, power, or madness, and House Caerthain may no longer be entirely human after centuries beside it. [[Prince Deyric Caerthain]] sailed onto this lake and never returned, and is said to speak to the current rulers in their sleep.

entries.name: Skyward Bastions
entries.summary: Armored watch-fortresses mounted on cliffs, repositioned by levitation crystals.
entries.sourceNote: Listed under Legacy of Craft & Power in The Duke's Family record.
entries.body:
Armored watch-fortresses mounted along the cliffs of the [[Cloudspine Ridge]], built to be moved. Early levitation crystals let a bastion be repositioned for tactical advantage — a fortification that does not have to stay where the enemy last saw it.

They are the first of the Caerthain crafts, and the reason the house's later work on airships surprised nobody who had seen the walls fly.

entries.name: The Vaulted Court
entries.summary: The Merca seat — part palace, part high-security financial centre.
entries.sourceNote: Named as the Seat of Power in The Merca Family record.
entries.body:
An opulent estate built above and within the [[Mithril Reserve]] itself: part palace, part vault, and entirely deliberate.

The [[The Merca Family - Marquis”|Merca]] did not build beside the bank. They built into it, so that reaching the family and reaching the money became the same problem.

entries.name: The Immortals
entries.summary: Acheaoria's elite unit — for every warrior fallen, two were said to rise.
entries.sourceNote: Named in the Acheaoria record.
entries.body:
The elite unit of the [[Acheaoria]] army, and the reason the empire's territorial losses in the [[Continental War]] never became a collapse.

They were trained to embody unwavering resolve and likened to a hydra: for every warrior who fell, two were said to rise in his place. Acheaoria lost vast ground in that war and paid a heavy toll in its people. The Immortals are what it did not lose.

Whether the comparison describes discipline, numbers, or something less ordinary is not settled in the record.

entries.name: The Argentar
entries.summary: The licensed, public-facing bankers of the Mithril Reserve.
entries.sourceNote: Described under Core Concepts in the Mithril Reserve record.
entries.body:
An Argentar is the face the [[Mithril Reserve]] shows the world: licensed, public, and answerable to the bank rather than to the client.

They are not tellers. An Argentar advises, assesses, and decides — a financial adviser and an agent of the Reserve in the same person, which are not always compatible roles.

Every major city has a stone branch, and every branch has its Argentar. They remember debts.

entries.name: The Serathian Fleet
entries.summary: Magically-augmented airships that descend into battle like hawks.
entries.sourceNote: Listed under Legacy of Craft & Power in The Duke's Family record.
entries.body:
Sleek, magically-augmented airships that sail the winds and drop into battle like hawks — founded, by the house's own account, by [[Empress-Lady Vaelis Caerthain]].

The Serathian Fleet is what turned [[The Duke's Family|House Caerthain]] from a house that held mountains into a house that commanded the sky above them. Their command of naval mountain craft and aerial engineering has kept them pioneers ever since.

Somewhere in the citadel there is a prototype called [[The Sovereign Star]].

entries.name: The Council of Eronis
entries.summary: Dream-walkers and illusionists believed to have ruled Nethrana.
entries.sourceNote: Named in The Truth — Notable as the believed rulers of Eronis.
entries.body:
Dream-walkers and illusionists, believed to have ruled from [[Eronis]] with an influence that ran well past the borders of [[Nethrana: The Kingdom of Mirrors and Mist|Nethrana]].

*Believed* is doing considerable work in that sentence. Nothing about the Council is attested directly — only inferred from the [[Palace of Eronis]], from portals rumoured to open onto dreamscapes, and from the fact that an empire of mirrors and mist must have been governed by someone.

**For the DM:** a council of dream-walkers does not necessarily stop governing just because its city fell.

entries.name: The Scholars
entries.summary: The body that classified the rifts into Bound, Shifting, and Anchored.
entries.sourceNote: Referenced in the Phenomenon record.
entries.body:
The Scholars are the authority that divided the rifts into three kinds — [[Bound Rifts]], [[Shifting Rifts]], and [[Anchored Rifts]] — and the reason anyone speaks about the [[Phenomenon]] in an orderly way at all.

Their records are also, in places, redacted. A body that catalogues holes in reality tends to accumulate findings it would rather not publish, and the gaps in the Scholars' own documents are as informative as the entries around them.

entries.name: The Pact
entries.summary: A treaty signed in enchanted water binding allied houses to eternal defence.
entries.sourceNote: Listed under Legacy of Craft & Power in The Duke's Family record.
entries.body:
A treaty signed in enchanted water, binding every allied house to the eternal defence of the empire and of its secrets.

The second clause is the one that matters. A pact that protects an empire is a military arrangement; a pact that protects an empire's *secrets* is something a party can be prosecuted under without ever having heard of it.

Signed in water, and therefore — the houses insist — not revocable by ink.

entries.name: The Continental War
entries.summary: The war that broke the old order and made the three empires what they are.
entries.sourceNote: Named across the Acheaoria, Hellenoria, and Duke's Family records (also called the War of the Continent).
entries.body:
The war every surviving empire dates itself from, and the one none of them describes the same way.

[[Acheaoria]] began it. Their conquests had carried them across nearly seventy percent of the continent before ambition ignited the war that cost them most of it — vast territories lost, a heavy toll on their people, and the [[The Immortals|Immortals]] left as proof that the army itself never broke.

[[Hellenoria]] was ravaged by it. Towns were destroyed, survivors abandoned their homes and converged on the capital, and what they pooled there became the basis of the empire that followed. [[Astraphael]] rose out of that convergence.

In the south, [[The Duke's Family|House Caerthain]] held the [[Cloudspine Ridge]] against a coalition of invading empires and earned its nobility doing it.

The records also call it *the War of the Continent*. Which name a source uses is often a reliable indication of where it was written.

entries.name: Bound Rifts
entries.summary: Rifts stable enough to cross safely — for as long as they last.
entries.sourceNote: Classified in the Phenomenon record.
entries.body:
The first of the three classifications made by [[The Scholars]]. A Bound Rift is stable enough that creatures pass freely between worlds with no apparent repercussion.

*Apparent* is the operative word, and *stable* is not the same as permanent — the lifespan of a Bound Rift varies enormously, and nothing in the record explains what sets it.

See also [[Shifting Rifts]], [[Anchored Rifts]], and the wider [[Phenomenon]].

entries.name: Shifting Rifts
entries.summary: Unpredictable rifts that cannot be entered and do not forgive the attempt.
entries.sourceNote: Classified in the Phenomenon record.
entries.body:
The second classification made by [[The Scholars]], and the one that killed people to establish.

Shifting Rifts appear suddenly and without warning. Unlike [[Bound Rifts]], no living creature of this world can enter one: those who have tried escaped barely, and came back marked in ways no scholar has been able to account for.

The marks are the part worth remembering. Something on the other side reached back.

entries.name: Anchored Rifts
entries.summary: The third classification of rift recognised by the Scholars.
entries.sourceNote: Named as the third rift type in the Phenomenon record.
entries.body:
The third of the classifications made by [[The Scholars]], alongside [[Bound Rifts]] and [[Shifting Rifts]].

The surviving record names the category and then says markedly less about it than about the other two — a silence that sits oddly next to the redactions elsewhere in the [[Phenomenon]] file.

**For the DM:** the source material leaves Anchored Rifts open. The name suggests something fixed in place, and fixed things can be found, guarded, or owned.

entries.name: Runes of Trust
entries.summary: Magical contracts that burn away when broken and cannot be forged.
entries.sourceNote: Listed under Legacy of Craft in The Merca Family record.

fields.properties: Cannot be forged; burns away on breach

entries.body:
A contract written in runes that cannot be forged and will not survive its own violation — break the terms and the document burns away.

The [[The Merca Family - Marquis”|Merca]] made their name on this craft. A Rune of Trust does not enforce a debt; it simply removes any argument about whether the debt was agreed.

**At the table:** the destruction is the notification. Everyone holding a counterpart knows the moment a party breaches.

entries.name: Ledgerlocks
entries.summary: Enchanted ledgers that open only to blood-bound members and verified heirs.
entries.sourceNote: Listed under Legacy of Craft in The Merca Family record.

fields.properties: Legible only to blood-bound members and verified heirs

entries.body:
Enchanted ledgers that reveal their contents to blood-bound members of the house and to verified heirs, and to nobody else. Stolen, a Ledgerlock is a blank book.

It follows that the [[The Merca Family - Marquis”|Merca]] can be robbed of their records without being robbed of their secrets — and that an heir is worth considerably more to a thief than a vault is.

entries.name: The Sovereign Star
entries.summary: A prototype airship held among House Caerthain's family secrets.
entries.sourceNote: Named under Family Secrets in The Duke's Family record.
entries.body:
A prototype airship, listed among the things [[The Duke's Family|House Caerthain]] does not discuss.

The house built [[The Serathian Fleet]] in the open and was celebrated for it. The Sovereign Star is filed with the lake, the worship, and the question of whether the bloodline is still human — which suggests it is not simply a faster vessel.

**For the DM:** the source gives you a name and a category and nothing else. That is a gift; decide what it does when the party needs it to matter.

entries.name: Commander Daud, The Royal Protector
entries.summary: Commander of the Adamantine Line, the legion of the Duneforged Citadel.
entries.sourceNote: Named in The Iron Parade Grounds record.
entries.body:
Commander of [[The Adamantine Line]] and nicknamed *the Royal Protector* — a title that says plainly whose person, rather than whose walls, he is expected to keep.

He holds the [[The Iron Parade Grounds|Iron Parade Grounds]] and a legion older than the primordial brood, whose reputation has been tempered by decades of war. Beneath him serves [[Vice-Commander Meagan Foster]].

A commander given a nickname by the ranks is usually one they would follow. A commander given one by the court is a different matter.

entries.name: Vice-Commander Meagan Foster
entries.summary: Second in command of the Adamantine Line.
entries.sourceNote: Named in The Iron Parade Grounds record.
entries.body:
Second to [[Commander Daud, The Royal Protector|Commander Daud]] in [[The Adamantine Line]], and the officer who actually runs a legion whose commander is occupied with protecting a royal person.

The record gives her the rank and nothing else, which in a legion of this age is its own kind of statement: the Line has outlasted every commander it ever had, and it did so because someone was minding it.

entries.name: Overseer Tarnak
entries.summary: Foreman of the Lower Mines, and a man with a problem underground.
entries.sourceNote: Named as a quest client in the Quests document.
entries.body:
Foreman of the lower shafts of [[The Dune Mines]], and currently the man responsible for an operation that has stopped.

Deep tremors and a low, unsettling hum have brought work in the lower levels to a halt. Tarnak needs it explained and he needs it explained quietly, because a mine that stays shut stops paying wages.

**Hook:** he will hire the party to go down and find the source of the hum. He would prefer they came back.

entries.name: The Adamantine Line
entries.summary: The legion of the Duneforged Citadel, older than the primordial brood.
entries.sourceNote: Fills an existing entry; described in The Iron Parade Grounds record.
entries.body:
The legion of the [[Duneforged Citadel]], quartered at [[The Iron Parade Grounds]].

The Line was raised before the primordial brood, and its reputation and prowess have been tempered across decades of war since. It is commanded by [[Commander Daud, The Royal Protector|Commander Daud]], with [[Vice-Commander Meagan Foster]] beneath him.

A formation that predates the brood has, by definition, survived whatever the brood was.

entries.name: The Dune Mines
entries.summary: Workings beneath the eastern slopes, where the lower shafts have fallen silent.
entries.sourceNote: Fills an existing entry; described in the Quests document.
entries.body:
Mine workings beneath the eastern slopes, outside the walls of the [[Duneforged Citadel]].

The upper levels run as they always have. The lower shafts do not: deep tremors and a low, continuous hum have stopped work entirely, and [[Overseer Tarnak]] has been unable to get anyone to go back down.

A hum is not a collapse. Collapses stop.

entries.name: Citadel Cathedral
entries.summary: The cathedral of the Duneforged Citadel, housing its temples.
entries.sourceNote: Exists in the export only as a database heading with no page of its own; its temples are its child records.
entries.body:
The cathedral of the [[Duneforged Citadel]], and the roof under which the citadel keeps its gods.

Its temples are held separately rather than as altars in a single nave — [[Forge of Vulcan]], [[Temple of Juno]], [[Vault of Mercury]], [[Shrine of Anchiale]], and the [[Sanctum of Hoplodamus]]. Between them they cover craft, oath, trade, fire, and the guardianship owed to those who fight at [[The Ju Colliseum]].

That a citadel ruled by [[The Duke's Family|House Caerthain]] should honour a god of creation and a god of binding oaths in the same building is not an accident of architecture.

entries.name: Forge of Vulcan
entries.summary: A temple of the Citadel Cathedral, kept for the Artisan of Creation.
entries.sourceNote: Fills an existing entry; filed under Citadel Cathedral / The Temples.
entries.body:
One of the temples of the [[Citadel Cathedral]] in the [[Duneforged Citadel]], kept for [[Vulcan, The Artisan of Creation|Vulcan]].

A house given to a god of creation, in a citadel whose nobility made its name on levitation crystals and airships, is not a quiet corner of the Cathedral. It is where the work is blessed.

entries.name: Temple of Juno
entries.summary: A temple of the Citadel Cathedral, kept for the Protector of Bonds.
entries.sourceNote: Fills an existing entry; filed under Citadel Cathedral / The Temples.
entries.body:
One of the temples of the [[Citadel Cathedral]] in the [[Duneforged Citadel]], kept for [[Juno, The Protector of Bonds|Juno]].

Oaths sworn here bind. In a citadel ruled by a house whose alliances rest on [[The Pact]] — a treaty signed in enchanted water — that is not a ceremonial function.

entries.name: Vault of Mercury
entries.summary: A temple of the Citadel Cathedral, kept for the Trickster of Trade.
entries.sourceNote: Fills an existing entry; filed under Citadel Cathedral / The Temples.
entries.body:
One of the temples of the [[Citadel Cathedral]] in the [[Duneforged Citadel]], kept for [[Mercury, The Trickster of Trade|Mercury]].

It is called a vault rather than a shrine, which for a god of both trade and trickery is either an act of devotion or a precaution.

entries.name: Shrine of Anchiale
entries.summary: A temple of the Citadel Cathedral, kept for the Flame Artisan.
entries.sourceNote: Fills an existing entry; filed under Citadel Cathedral / The Temples.
entries.body:
One of the temples of the [[Citadel Cathedral]] in the [[Duneforged Citadel]], kept for [[Anchiale, The Flame Artisan|Anchiale]].

The Ju Colliseum names Anchiale for adaptability and cunning. A titan of fire and craft honoured in a mountain citadel of smiths is an obvious patron — the cunning is the part worth watching.

entries.name: Sanctum of Hoplodamus
entries.summary: A temple of the Citadel Cathedral, kept for the Titan of Guardianship.
entries.sourceNote: Fills an existing entry; filed under Citadel Cathedral / The Temples.
entries.body:
One of the temples of the [[Citadel Cathedral]] in the [[Duneforged Citadel]], kept for [[Hoplodamus, Titan of Guardianship|Hoplodamus]].

The trials fought at [[The Ju Colliseum]] are held sacred before Hoplodamus, and those who fight well there may be granted divine mercy — which the record defines as a fast, clean death.

The guardianship offered in this sanctum is of that kind.

entries.name: Healer's Sanctuary
entries.summary: The house of healing within the Duneforged Citadel.
entries.sourceNote: Fills an existing entry; filed under Duneforged Citadel / Locations.
entries.body:
The house of healing of the [[Duneforged Citadel]], standing among its named locations rather than among the temples of the [[Citadel Cathedral]].

A citadel that keeps [[The Adamantine Line]] and runs [[The Ju Colliseum]] generates a steady supply of the wounded. The Sanctuary is where they are brought.

entries.name: The Aletheion
entries.summary: The Imperial Mouseion of Helarchon — the history of the city in five rooms, told the way the censors allow.
entries.sourceNote: Authored for the one-shot 'The Aletheion Heist' (docs/oneshots/the-aletheion-heist.md); grounded in the Hellenoria chronicle and the Mycairos record.
entries.body:
On Museum Hill in the Scholars' District of [[Hellarchon City]], in the violet shadow of the Arcane Academy, stands the Imperial Mouseion: **the Aletheion**, from the old tongue's *alētheia* — truth, literally *un-forgetting*. The wags of the city call it the *Lētheion*, the House of Forgetting, because every label in the building has been through the censors. Both names are truer than the curators would like.

It is the history of [[Hellenoria]]'s capital told in five rooms — the approved version. [[Selenarion of Helarchon]] drafted the labels; the Truth-Flame rewrote them.

**Rotunda of the Concord.** The founding mosaic — settlers of every trade laying down tools together — beneath a domed skylight, watched by four Mycairan bronze hoplites the staff quietly re-pose every dawn.

**Founders' Hall.** The Oath-Prow of the first settler ship, votive nets and mining lamps of the first trades, and the Thalos Stele, labelled a *ceremonial ossuary marker*.

**Hall of the Storm-Star.** [[The Continental War]], and the man who ended Hellenoria's part in it: the storm-scored half-mantle of [[Astraphael, the Destructive Star]], an illuminated facsimile of the Treaty of Myrianth, the Silent Sail — cut from a ship of the fleet, damp and cold to this day — and a shattered blade whose plinth has had a name chiseled out of it.

**Gallery of the Violet Dusk.** Aetherglass panes from "the old harbor fire" that show yesterday's sky rather than today's, and the Academy's dusk prisms.

**The Bronze Vault.** Everything raised from the Thalos Ridge dig into the ruins of [[Mycairos: The Kingdom of Bronze and Blood]] that is too dangerous or too true for upstairs — rune tablets repeating *the gift beneath stone*, a weeping colossus head, and the museum's star exhibit: the [[Kleis Mycarion]], suspended inside the Academy's Seal of the Fourth Mirror.

A Sealed Annex on the upper floor holds the proscribed manuscripts, in Truth-Flame custody. Museum staff do not go up there.

entries.name: Kleis Mycarion
entries.summary: The Key of Mycarion — bronze wound around bone, warm, with something like a heartbeat — raised from the ruins beneath Thalos Ridge.
entries.sourceNote: Authored for the one-shot 'The Aletheion Heist'; extends the 'gift beneath stone' thread in the Mycairos record.

fields.type: Relic — Divine? Infernal? The runes decline to say
fields.price: No listed value; there is exactly one buyer
fields.attunement: None — and the Academy advises against bare-skin contact
fields.properties: Forearm-long key of layered bronze wound around what is probably bone. Warm to the touch; a slow pulse, roughly one beat per breath. Anyone who holds it skin-to-skin dreams of Thalos Ridge that night and must succeed on a DC 12 Wisdom save each dawn or spend the day knowing exactly which direction the ridge lies.

entries.body:
Three years ago an Academy dig beneath **Thalos Ridge** broke into an under-citadel of [[Mycairos: The Kingdom of Bronze and Blood]], and among the bronze they raised was a key.

The runes of Mycairos repeat one phrase scholars still cannot close the book on: *the gift beneath stone*. The Kleis Mycarion is, as far as anyone can prove, a key without a lock — but two conservators who handled it began sleepwalking toward the ridge, and the Arcane Academy does not seal exhibits for nothing. It now hangs suspended inside the **Seal of the Fourth Mirror** in the Bronze Vault of [[The Aletheion]]: four counter-rotating rings of mirrored glass in which the reflected room is always slightly wrong.

What it opens is the question. The Academy files say nothing. The occult societies of [[Hellenoria]] — [[The Eclipsed Mirror]] loudest among them, in the whispers where such societies are loud — believe the gift beneath stone is a door, and that doors of that kind belong to [[Hecate, The Mistress of the Arcane]].

Whatever emptied Mycairos in a single generation was beneath stone the whole time.

entries.name: The Lysikleis
entries.summary: A handleless memorysteel key that learns the shape of any lock or seal pressed against it — Virellarion work, bought through the black market.
entries.sourceNote: Authored for the one-shot 'The Aletheion Heist'; the memorysteel is Virellarion craft per the family record.

fields.properties: Pressed against a lock, glyph, or seal for 1 minute, the Lysikleis learns its shape. Expend 1 charge to open that lock or suppress that seal or glyph for 1 hour. 2 charges remain; it does not recharge. It hums, very slightly, like it is thinking.

entries.body:
*Lysikleis* — "the loosening key" — is a handleless key of **memorysteel**, the metal that remembers its last shape, and unmistakably the work of [[The Virellarion Family - Count]]: no one else's steel *thinks*.

It was commissioned quietly, paid for in full, and left waiting at a fence's stall in the Night Agora — the masked black market [[The Obsidian Masquerade]] throws beneath the Old Harbor of [[Hellarchon City]], where the [[Tenebral Covenant]] honors purchases and [[The Nightweaver Syndicate]] watches who collects them.

The buyer was [[The Eclipsed Mirror]], and the shape the key was born to learn is the Arcane Academy's Seal of the Fourth Mirror — the four rings of mirrored glass around the [[Kleis Mycarion]] in [[The Aletheion]]. A tool built a year in advance, for a theft that would take one night.

entries.name: Madame Trioditis
entries.summary: Broker of the Eclipsed Mirror — a changeling who is three people, and counts the questions you ask her on her fingers.
entries.sourceNote: Authored for the one-shot 'The Aletheion Heist'; named for Hecate's epithet of the three roads.
entries.body:
The veiled widow in the harbor taverna, the fishmonger at the dead-drop, and the lamplighter on Museum Hill's lower stair are the same person. Madame Trioditis — named for the three roads of [[Hecate, The Mistress of the Arcane]] — is the public hand of [[The Eclipsed Mirror]], insofar as a society like the Mirror can be said to have one.

She speaks in threes. She answers exactly three questions honestly per meeting, and counts them on her fingers. She wears a silver ring set with a disc of black mirror, smells of myrrh and rain, and pays what she promises to the coin — her circle's credit is good from the Night Agora to the [[Tenebral Covenant]]'s ledgers, which in [[Hellarchon City]]'s underworld is worth more than a temple oath.

When she hires a crew she tells them three rules: don't kill anyone, don't be seen taking it, and don't — under any circumstances — touch the [[Kleis Mycarion]] with bare skin. She would prefer not to break her tools. She has others.

entries.name: Inquisitor Callixta Vireon
entries.summary: Truth-Flame inquisitor, blood-heir to the Third Seat, who audits the Aletheion's labels until they say what is required.
entries.sourceNote: Authored for the one-shot 'The Aletheion Heist'; continues the line of the Inquisitor Vireon who annotated Selenarion's chronicle.

fields.role: Inquisitor of the Truth-Flame, blood-heir to the Third Seat
fields.statblock: Priest (flame-flavored). HP 38, AC 13 (16 with shield of faith). Sacred flame 2d8 (DC 13 Dex); mace +2 (1d6). Truth-Flame Brand: bonus action, one creature she can see, DC 13 Wis or it cannot hide from her for 10 minutes. Attended by two templars (guards, HP 22, AC 16, flame-tipped maces 1d6+1 plus 2 fire).

entries.body:
The margins of the chronicle [[Selenarion of Helarchon]] left behind carry the annotations of an Inquisitor Vireon, Third Seat of the Truth-Flame — *this passage is to be struck from all Temple copies*. Callixta Vireon is that line's blood-heir, and the family trade has not changed: history in [[Hellenoria]] says what the Truth-Flame requires it to say.

She works out of the Sealed Annex of [[The Aletheion]], where the proscribed manuscripts are kept, and on the eve of any exhibition she audits every label in the building until dawn. She is ash-grey, precise, and carries a brand-iron the way a priest carries a holy symbol.

She wants arrests and confessions, not corpses — a dead thief confesses nothing. But she holds one hatred above her hatred of thieves: unsanctioned bronze walking the halls is *heresy*, and the night the Bronze Vault's exhibits remember what they were for, every flame she has turns that way first.

entries.name: The Aletheion Heist
entries.summary: An occult society hires a deniable crew to steal the sealed Kleis Mycarion from the Imperial Mouseion — on the one night it can be done.
entries.sourceNote: Authored one-shot; the full module with map, timelines, and stat blocks lives in docs/oneshots/the-aletheion-heist.md.

fields.reward: 1,500 gp total (300 gp each — a fair 1,000 gp rate plus a 50% hazard premium for the seal): 600 gp advance, 900 gp on delivery, or swap the 900 for two divinity-infused Drachmae stamped with Hecate's triple face. The crew keeps the Lysikleis if a charge remains.

entries.body:
A one-shot for five 4th-level characters, roughly four hours. The full module — museum map, Lantern Clock, patrol schedules, exhibits with fence values, stat blocks — lives in `docs/oneshots/the-aletheion-heist.md`.

**The job.** [[The Eclipsed Mirror]] believes the [[Kleis Mycarion]] opens *the gift beneath stone* — the door the runes of [[Mycairos: The Kingdom of Bronze and Blood]] would not name — and that doors of that kind belong to [[Hecate, The Mistress of the Arcane]]. Their broker, [[Madame Trioditis]], hires the crew with three rules: no killing, no witnesses to the taking, and no bare skin on the key.

**Act I — the Night Agora.** The seal-breaker is already bought and paid for: [[The Lysikleis]], waiting at a [[Tenebral Covenant]] stall inside the masked revel [[The Obsidian Masquerade]] throws beneath the Old Harbor. Entry costs a truth spoken aloud at the door. A moth-masked broker of [[The Nightweaver Syndicate]] offers double to walk the key elsewhere — and picks pockets when refused.

**Act II — casing the Aletheion.** [[The Aletheion]] is closed for re-labeling on the eve of its Treaty of Myrianth anniversary exhibition; at dawn the Kleis moves to the Academy deep-vaults forever. Skeleton watch, a bribeable warden with dice debts, [[Inquisitor Callixta Vireon]] auditing the Sealed Annex all night — and three ways in: forged credentials at the service dock, the flooded rain-cistern beneath Museum Hill, or the rotunda skylight.

**Act III — the heist.** The Seal of the Fourth Mirror marks anyone who reaches through it for Academy scrying; the Lysikleis unwinds it clean. But the moment the key leaves its plinth, every Mycairan bronze in the building remembers what it was for — and the escape matters more than the fight. A [[Tenebral Covenant]] crew is robbing the Founders' Hall the same night; the [[Crimson Pact]] is who the Mirror sends if the crew keeps the key.

**Delivery.** Trioditis pays in coin or [[Drachmae]], takes the wrapped key, and asks one question she means: *"Did it whisper to any of you?"* The road to Thalos Ridge is the sequel.
